title: The Smallest Sum of a Falling Path

concept.title: Each cell looks at up to three cells of the row above
body: A table of numbers (possibly negative) is given. A *falling path* starts at any cell of the **top row** and moves down one row at a time: from the cell `(i, j)` it may go to `(i + 1, j - 1)`, `(i + 1, j)` or `(i + 1, j + 1)` (as long as the column exists). Find the smallest sum of the numbers on a falling path that reaches the bottom row.

Let `best(i, j)` be the smallest sum of a falling path that **ends** in the cell `(i, j)`. In the top row it is the number itself. A path to `(i, j)` came from one of the three cells above, so **`best(i, j) = value(i, j) + min of best(i - 1, j - 1), best(i - 1, j), best(i - 1, j + 1)`**, using only the cells that exist. The answer is the smallest value in the last row, because the path may end anywhere.

Here we cannot overwrite in place, because a cell needs the **old** values of both neighbours; so we build a new row each time (or keep one old row and one new row). The time is O(h * w), the memory O(w). The only change from the route problems is the free choice of the start and the end, and one more neighbour.

statement: A table has `h` rows and `w` columns. A falling path starts at any cell of the first row and moves to the next row each step, going to the cell directly below or to one of the two diagonal neighbours below (if it exists). Print the smallest possible sum of the numbers on a path that reaches the last row.
inputFormat: The first line has `h` and `w`: the number of rows and columns.
Each of the next `h` lines has `w` numbers: one row of the table.

examples.note: The path 1, 5, 7 has the sum 13 (so has 1, 4, 8), and no path is cheaper.
A single row: the smallest number, -2.

hints: Let best(i, j) be the smallest sum of a falling path that ends in the cell (i, j).
Take the smallest of the up to three cells above and add the value of the cell.
The answer is the smallest value in the last row.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

h, w = map(int, input().split())
matrix = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(h)]

# Your code here

explanation: best(i, j) = value(i, j) + the smallest of the up to three cells above, row by row; the answer is the smallest value of the last row.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

h, w = map(int, input().split())
matrix = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(h)]

best = matrix[0][:]
for i in range(1, h):
    row = matrix[i]
    new = [0] * w
    for j in range(w):
        lowest = best[j]
        if j > 0 and best[j - 1] < lowest:
            lowest = best[j - 1]
        if j + 1 < w and best[j + 1] < lowest:
            lowest = best[j + 1]
        new[j] = lowest + row[j]
    best = new
print(min(best))
